title: IFERROR: catch the error, show your text

screens.prompt: In B5, look up the price of the SKU in A4, and show "no price" if the lookup fails.

hints.syntax: IFERROR takes the thing that might fail, then what to show instead: =IFERROR(lookup, "no price").
hints.func-iferror: IFERROR wraps the lookup and supplies the words; the lookup on its own returns #N/A and the cell reads as an error.
hints.require-ref: Ask about the SKU in A4 instead of typing TX-109, so the question can be changed in one cell.
hints.value: TX-109 is not in the list, so the cell should read the fallback text the prompt asks for.
hints.error: IFERROR catches errors inside it, not errors you make outside it: adding one to the fallback text still returns #VALUE!.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
the bare lookup returns #N/A, which is the error this lesson exists to replace
one argument leaves IFERROR with nothing to show when the lookup fails
nothing in that can fail, so the answer is the SKU itself
the fallback is the text you pass, and the prompt asked for no price
the SKU typed into the formula, so asking about another SKU means editing the formula
the fallback text is then added to a number outside the protection, and #VALUE! comes back

docs.explain: The list holds TX-101 and TX-102, and A4 asks about TX-109, so the lookup finds nothing and returns #N/A. IFERROR takes two arguments: the calculation that might fail, and what to show when it does. Wrapped around the lookup, the cell reads no price, which is a sentence someone can act on. IFERROR catches every error type, not only a missed lookup. #REF!, #VALUE! and #DIV/0! all get the same fallback, which is convenient and can hide a real mistake: a broken reference now looks like a missing price. It only protects what is inside it, so arithmetic done outside the wrapper can still return an error.

errors.text: A lookup found nothing and no fallback was supplied, so the cell shows the error rather than a sentence.
Arithmetic was done on the fallback text after IFERROR had already returned it.

docs.atWork: A price sheet shared with a customer, where a discontinued SKU has to read as missing rather than showing an error code.
docs.outcome: Replace an error with text you chose, and know what that hides.
docs.dataset: Two prices and a missing SKU

seo.title: IFERROR in Excel: replace an error with text
seo.description: A lookup for TX-109 finds nothing and returns #N/A. IFERROR shows text you choose instead, which reads better and can also hide a real mistake.
